sections.h2: What is the option period in a Texas home sale contract?
sections.html:
It is a window in which a buyer who paid an agreed option fee can end the contract for any reason by giving the seller written notice. TREC's FAQ describes it that way and adds that the termination option is a negotiable term, so a buyer does not have to pay for one.

Buyers typically use the days to inspect the house and negotiate repairs through an amendment, or to walk away. For a seller, the period is the stretch in which the deal can end without the buyer giving a reason, so the numbers written into the contract matter.

sections.h2: Which TREC contract form is used for a resale in 2026?
sections.html:
The One to Four Family Residential Contract (Resale), Form 20-19, with an effective date of July 1, 2026. TREC calls it the most frequently used contract form, for the resale of a single family home, duplex, triplex or fourplex.

TREC says it is not for condominium sales, new homes sold by a builder, or farm and ranch property, and TREC publishes separate forms for those. The Commission's contracts page lists many addenda alongside it, including a third party financing addendum, a seller financing addendum, a short sale addendum and a back-up contract addendum.

sections.h2: How do the option fee and earnest money work?
sections.html:
The buyer delivers earnest money and the option fee to the escrow agent. TREC's FAQ quotes paragraph 5A of an earlier edition of the form as requiring delivery within three days of the effective date, and quotes paragraph 5D for the consequence: if no option fee amount is stated or the buyer fails to deliver it on time, the buyer has no unrestricted right to terminate under that paragraph.

Because the FAQ quotes an earlier edition, read the paragraph numbers and day counts in the current 20-19 itself, or ask your agent or title company to point them out. TREC counts days from the effective date, with the first day being the next day, and each day is a calendar day.

  • Option fee: set by the parties, paid to the seller for the termination right.
  • Earnest money: held by the escrow agent.
  • Option days: a negotiated number written into the contract.
  • Notice: written, delivered to the other side.

sections.h2: How are days counted when a contract has deadlines?
sections.html:
TREC's FAQ says the count starts with the effective date, which is the date of final signature, and the first day of any period is the day after. Every day is a calendar day, so weekends and holidays count. A seller who signs on a Friday should see that the next day is day one, and should ask the agent to mark the end date on a calendar.

Notices tied to a deadline should be sent in the manner the contract's notice paragraph requires, and a missed deadline can change what a party may do. Because TREC does not decide whether a contract is valid or which party wins a dispute, keep a dated copy of every notice sent or received.

sections.h2: What if the buyer never paid earnest money?
sections.html:
TREC says its forms require the buyer to deliver earnest money to the escrow agent, and if the buyer does not deliver it on time, the seller may terminate or exercise remedies under the contract's default paragraph. TREC adds that it has no jurisdiction to decide who is entitled to earnest money.

If a dispute over earnest money arises, TREC points people to a private attorney, and says it has no authority over title companies. It can take complaints about a license holder who fails to deposit earnest money as the contract requires.

sections.h2: What must a Texas seller disclose?
sections.html:
Texas sellers of previously occupied single family homes complete the Seller's Disclosure Notice, TREC Form 55-1, which carries an effective date of May 28, 2026 on TREC's page. TREC says the form covers information required by Section 5.008 of the Property Code about material facts and the physical condition of the property, and applies with a contract entered into on or after September 1, 2023.

Give the notice completely and accurately, and ask your agent how to answer any question about repairs or known defects. TREC's FAQ warns that a mistake in completing a form can lead to financial loss or an unenforceable contract.

sections.h2: How do repair terms and the option period fit together?
sections.html:
TREC's FAQ says a buyer should check the box for specific repairs only if particular repairs are known when the contract is signed. Otherwise the buyer checks the as-is box, and most buyers then pay for an option period to inspect and negotiate.

Repair paths described in TREC's FAQ
SituationWhat TREC says to do
Specific repairs known at signingUse the specific-repairs choice and list them
No known repairsUse the as-is choice
Repairs found by inspectionAmend the contract, or terminate during the option period
Boxes left blank or vagueNot permitted, per TREC

For a seller, this means repair requests usually come through an amendment after the buyer inspects, and the option period is the time that bargaining happens.

sections.h2: Can I use a TREC form without an agent?
sections.html:
Yes. TREC's FAQ says the contract forms are available for public use, but they are intended primarily for brokers and sales agents trained in using them. It warns that a mistake in using a form may lead to financial loss or an unenforceable contract, and that a person using a form accepts all risks that come with it.

The FAQ says a license holder who fills in a form may add only factual matters and business details to a form adopted for mandatory use. If TREC has not promulgated a form that you need, TREC says to have an attorney draft it, and it notes that a license holder may not draft an instrument that transfers or affects an interest in real property.

  • A Texas real estate attorney can draft terms the forms do not cover.
  • Members of the Texas Association of Realtors can use that group's forms.
  • Your title company can answer how it handles earnest money and the option fee.

sections.h2: What should a seller check in the signed contract?
sections.html:
Before you sign a Texas contract, find the option days, the option fee, the earnest money amount and the repair choice. These are blanks or checkboxes that parties fill in, and TREC's FAQ treats complete and accurate completion as the license holder's duty.

  • The effective date is filled in.
  • The option fee amount is stated, and a due date for delivery.
  • The earnest money amount and the escrow agent are named.
  • The repair paragraph has one choice marked, not both and not neither.
  • Any addendum, such as financing or a back-up contract, is attached.

TREC says it cannot decide whether a contract with a blank effective date is valid. That question goes to a private attorney, so catch blanks before signing.

sections.h2: Can I end the contract, and who gets help with the paperwork?
sections.html:
A buyer who wants to terminate can use TREC's Notice of Buyer's Termination of Contract form, and a seller has a matching Notice of Seller's Termination form. TREC publishes both. Notices need to reach the other side in the way the contract requires, so check the notice paragraph in your form.

TREC's FAQ says license holders must use adopted contract forms and may add only factual matters and business details. It also says no TREC form is meant to be a contract for deed, and that anyone who needs something the forms do not cover should have an attorney prepare it. TREC does not decide whether a contract is valid, so a blank effective date or a disputed term goes to a private attorney.

faqs.q: Is an option period required in a Texas home contract?
faqs.a: No. TREC says the termination option is a negotiable term and a buyer does not have to pay for one. A buyer who pays the agreed fee gets the right to terminate for any reason by written notice during the option period.

faqs.q: How long is the option period?
faqs.a: The parties negotiate it, and it is written into the contract. TREC's FAQ gives no standard length, so check the number in your signed form.

faqs.q: What if the buyer did not pay the option fee?
faqs.a: Probably no unrestricted termination right. TREC's FAQ quotes the form as saying a buyer who states no fee or fails to deliver it on time loses that right under the option paragraph.

faqs.q: Which form applies to my Texas house sale?
faqs.a: Form 20-19, effective July 1, 2026, for single family homes and two to four unit residential properties. TREC lists separate forms for condos, new builds and farm and ranch property.

faqs.q: Can TREC decide an earnest money dispute?
faqs.a: No. TREC says it lacks jurisdiction over who is entitled to earnest money, and refers parties to a private attorney.
